value: カウボーイビバップ (Kaubōi Bibappu)
text: In Japanese the title is カウボーイビバップ, read Kaubōi Bibappu, a katakana version of Cowboy Bebop.
excerpt: Cowboy Bebop (カウボーイビバップ, Kaubōi Bibappu)

value: Sunrise (studio), Shinichirō Watanabe (director)
text: Sunrise made the series, with Shinichirō Watanabe leading the team as director.
excerpt: Created and animated by Sunrise, it was led by a production team of director Shinichirō Watanabe

value: Hajime Yatate (collective pen name)
text: The credited creator Hajime Yatate is not one person but a shared pen name for the Sunrise staff.
excerpt: Hajime Yatate, the well-known pseudonym for the collective contributions of Sunrise's animation staff

value: 26 episodes (called sessions), 1 season
text: The series is a single season of 26 episodes, which the show calls sessions.
excerpt: The series, which ran for twenty-six episodes (dubbed "sessions")

value: April 3 to June 26, 1998 (TV Tokyo)
text: TV Tokyo aired the show first, from 3 April to 26 June 1998, before the full run reached Wowow.
excerpt: The show's first run, from April 3 until June 26, 1998, on TV Tokyo

value: Wowow, 23 October 1998 to 24 April 1999 (complete run)
text: Satellite channel Wowow showed all of it from 23 October 1998 to 24 April 1999.
excerpt: the series was shown in its entirety from October 23, 1998, to April 24, 1999, on the satellite network Wowow

value: Year 2071; bounty hunters aboard the spaceship Bebop
text: In 2071 a crew of bounty hunters, nicknamed cowboys, chase criminals around the Solar System from a ship called the Bebop.
excerpt: is set in the year 2071 and follows the lives of a traveling bounty-hunting crew aboard a spaceship, the Bebop

value: Yoko Kanno, with the band Seatbelts
text: Yoko Kanno scored the show in a jazz-heavy style and formed the band Seatbelts to play it.
excerpt: Kanno formed the blues and jazz band Seatbelts to perform the music

value: Tank! - Seatbelts
text: The opening, Tank!, is a mostly instrumental big band number with a long alto saxophone solo by Masato Honda.
excerpt: "Tank!" is the series' opening song. The song, written by Yoko Kanno and performed by Seatbelts

value: The Real Folk Blues - Seatbelts featuring Mai Yamane
text: The first ending theme has vocals by Mai Yamane, and it is one of the few songs in the series sung in Japanese.
excerpt: "The Real Folk Blues" is the first ending theme for Cowboy Bebop

value: Cowboy Bebop: The Movie, Japan September 1, 2001, set between episodes 22 and 23, studio Bones with Sunrise
text: The film, called Knockin' on Heaven's Door in Japan, opened on 1 September 2001, takes place between episodes 22 and 23, and was animated by Bones for Sunrise.
excerpt: Set between episodes 22 and 23 of the original series

value: 1999 Anime Grand Prix: best male character (Spike Spiegel), best voice actor (Megumi Hayashibara)
text: At the 1999 Anime Grand Prix, which looked back on 1998, Spike Spiegel was voted best male character and Megumi Hayashibara, Faye's voice, best voice actor.
excerpt: Spike Spiegel was awarded the best male character; and Megumi Hayashibara was awarded the best voice actor

value: First anime shown on Adult Swim's launch night, September 2, 2001
text: When Adult Swim launched on 2 September 2001, Cowboy Bebop was the first anime on its schedule, at midnight Eastern.
excerpt: being the first anime shown on the block that night at midnight ET

value: Sessions 1 to 22
Cowboy Bebop: The Movie
Sessions 23 to 26
text: Because the film sits between episodes 22 and 23, the story here runs sessions 1 to 22, then the film, then sessions 23 to 26.
excerpt: The film takes place between episodes 22 and 23.

value: Spike Spiegel (スパイク・スピーゲル): a bounty hunter and ace pilot
Jet Black (ジェット・ブラック): the retired cop who owns the Bebop
Faye Valentine (フェイ・ヴァレンタイン): the amnesiac gambler in debt
Edward Wong Hau Pepelu Tivrusky IV (エドワード・ウォン・ハウ・ペペル・チブルスキー4世): the hacker prodigy known as Ed
Ein (アイン): the corgi data dog
Vicious (ビシャス): a Red Dragon Syndicate rival of Spike
Julia (ジュリア): a woman from Spike's past
Andy von de Oniyate: the cowboy-styled bounty hunter
Laughing Bull (ラフィング・ブル): the shaman on Mars
Gren Eckener: the former soldier in Jupiter Jazz
Vincent Volaju (ヴィンセント・ボラージュ): the film's terrorist
Electra Ovilo (エレクトラ・オヴィロゥ): the film's Titan War veteran
text: Twelve people and one dog from the series and the film, with their Japanese names where the sources give them.
excerpt: Spike Spiegel is a tall, lean, and slightly muscular 27-year-old bounty hunter born on Mars
